_comment: Tier-2 for sparta rarefied_flow: the four ways a per-cell diagnostic lies while the run exits 0 with no error and no warning. Six decks were run on the installed binary (SPARTA 24 Sep 2025, spa_serial), all the same 1 mm 2d argon box, differing only in grid resolution, fix ave/grid sample count, or timestep. rarefied_flow:1 — at step 0 the fix ave/grid has produced nothing and compute lambda/grid returns the BIG sentinel; and with a single-sample fix on a refined grid the Kn MAXIMUM stays pinned at the sentinel on every stats line while the Kn minimum reads a perfectly ordinary few, so reducing with min alone never sees it. rarefied_flow:3 — the 200x200 grid has a per-cell particle minimum of exactly 0 and still reports a plausible collision count. rarefied_flow:0 — the 5x5 grid has a cell Knudsen minimum below 1 (cells larger than a mean free path) while holding twenty times MORE particles per cell than the resolved grid, so a particle-count check passes on the broken case. rarefied_flow:2 — compute dt/grid returns the same recommendation whether the deck sets a timestep a hundred times larger or a hundred times smaller, a 10000x span, and the too-large one exits 0. rarefied_flow:7 — and none of it shows up in the collision column, because a box at rest has no gradient for the errors to act on: Ncoll spans a factor of nearly nine thousand across those runs while the collision RATE (Ncoll divided by the timestep that produced it) spans 1.13, and the 16x cell-count change moves the rate by 2 %. So a dt or grid study on an equilibrium box measures nothing. Nothing is asserted against a stored value: the sentinel is identified by being fifteen orders of magnitude from the healthy value IN THE SAME RUN, the resolution claims are comparisons between two grids, and the dt/grid and equilibrium claims are ratios between runs in this script. COVERS: rarefied_flow:0, :1, :2, :3, :7.
